'''William Craig Reynolds''' (March 16, 1933 – January 3, 2004) was a [[Fluid mechanics|fluid physicist]] and [[Mechanical engineering|mechanical engineer]] who specialized in [[Turbulence|turbulent flow]] and [[computational fluid dynamics]].<ref name="Moin">{{cite journal |last1=Moin |first1=Parviz |last2=Homsy |first2=G.M. |title=An Appreciation of the Life and Work of William C. Reynolds (1933–2004) |journal=Annual Review of Fluid Mechanics |date=3 January 2017 |volume=49 |issue=1 |pages=1–21 |doi=10.1146/annurev-fluid-122414-034434 |language=en |issn=0066-4189|doi-access=free |bibcode=2017AnRFM..49....1M }}</ref><ref name="Bradshaw">{{Citation
| doi = 10.1063/1.1955501
| volume = 58
| issue = 4
| pages = 85–86
| last = Bradshaw
| first = Peter
| title = William Craig Reynolds
| journal = Physics Today
| year = 2005
|bibcode = 2005PhT....58R..85B }}</ref>

Reynolds completed his undergraduate degrees, as well as his doctorate, all at [[Stanford University]], in 1954, 1955, and 1957, respectively, after which he joined the faculty. He was chairman of the Mechanical Engineering Department from 1972 to 1982 and again from 1989 to 1992.<ref name="moin_2007">{{citation |author-link=Parviz Moin |last=Moin |first=P. |year=2007 |title=William C. Reynolds |journal=Memorial Tributes: National Academy of Engineering |volume=11 |pages=266–269 |url=http://www.nap.edu/openbook.php?record_id=11912&page=266}}</ref>

Reynolds was one of the pioneers in [[Large eddy simulation]] for fluid modeling.<ref name="Moin"/><ref name="moin_2007"/> He was elected to the [[National Academy of Engineering]] in 1979.<ref name="Moin"/> He won the Fluid Engineering Award of the [[American Society of Mechanical Engineers]] in 1989<ref>{{cite web |title=Fluids Engineering Award |url=https://www.asme.org/about-asme/honors-awards/achievement-awards/fluids-engineering-award |website=American Society of Mechanical Engineers |access-date=27 March 2023 |language=en}}</ref> and the [[Otto Laporte Award]] by the [[American Physical Society]] in 1992.<ref>{{cite web |title=Prize Recipient |url=https://www.aps.org/programs/honors/prizes/prizerecipient.cfm?first_nm=William&last_nm=Reynolds&year=1992 |website=American Physical Society |access-date=27 March 2023 |language=en}}</ref>

Following his death, the Department of Mechanical Engineering at Stanford established the William C. Reynolds Memorial Award and Lecture.<ref>{{Cite web |date=November 3, 2004 |title=Stanofrd report |url=https://searchworks.stanford.edu/view/3057057 |access-date=2026-06-05 |website=searchworks.stanford.edu}}</ref>
